newsitem.title: USA: Foamex says Farace to succeed Cogan as CEO.
newsitem.headline: Foamex says Farace to succeed Cogan as CEO.

text.p: Foamex International said Monday it had appointed Andrea Farace, 41, to succeed Marshall Cogan as the company's chairman and chief executive officer, effective May 30.

Cogan, 59, the company's founder, will remain vice chairman, Foamex said, but acknowledged Cogan will be spending more time in New York to assume expanded duties at United Auto Group Inc - another company he founded.
"Mr Cogan lives in New York and will be spending more time there," a Foamex official said, after having assumed duties on April 17 as chairman and executive officer of United Auto Group.
Foamex said Farace, president of Trace International Holdings, Inc, has been a member of the Foamex board of directors since last year.
In other changes, Foamex said John Rallis, 59, who has served as president, chief operating officer and a director since 1994, is retiring from these positions.
The company said it had promoted Salvatore Bonanno, 56, as president, effective May 30.

Bonanno, who joined Foamex in mid-1995 and serves as executive vice president of manufacturing, will continue to oversee the company's manufacturing operations, Foamex said. (( New York Newsdesk, 212 859-1610))
